summary_en: Tokyo Electron Device raised interim and year-end dividend forecasts for fiscal year ending March 2027. Interim dividend set at ¥69 per share (up from ¥60 forecast); year-end dividend revised to ¥82 per share (up from ¥69 forecast), bringing total annual dividend forecast to ¥151 per share. Increases reflect upward revision of full-year consolidated earnings guidance driven by strong semiconductor and IT demand.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Full-Year Consolidated Earnings Forecast for Fiscal Year Ending March 2027 and Revision (Increase) of Dividend Forecast for Interim and Year-End Dividends as of September 30, 2026
translation_en_brief:
On October 28, 2026, Tokyo Electron Device announced an increase in its dividend forecasts for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, following an upward revision of consolidated earnings guidance. The interim dividend, based on September 30, 2026, was set at ¥69 per share, up ¥9 from the previously forecast ¥60 per share. The year-end dividend forecast was raised to ¥82 per share from ¥69 per share, resulting in a total annual dividend forecast of ¥151 per share, compared to the previous forecast of ¥129 per share.

The company increased full-year revenue guidance from ¥240 billion to ¥270 billion, ordinary profit from ¥13.6 billion to ¥16.0 billion, and net income attributable to parent company shareholders from ¥9.4 billion to ¥11.0 billion. These increases reflect robust demand for semiconductors and electronic devices, strong corporate IT investment, and continued high demand for semiconductor and IT products driven by AI expansion. While the company noted some product lines experienced extended lead times due to supplier constraints, it maintained a positive outlook for steady business progress through the end of the fiscal year.

The dividend increases align with the company's policy of targeting a consolidated payout ratio of approximately 40%, taking into account future capital expenditure needs, research and development funding requirements, and working capital trends.
